per_column.name: writing_quality_issue
per_column.rationale: Captures a candidate cause of dissatisfaction (weak screenplay, clichéd script, incoherent plot). This is a plausible treatment/cause whose effect on satisfaction is being attributed, surfaced from the review text rather than named in the generic 'why dissatisfied' query.

per_column.name: plot_originality_rating
per_column.rationale: Another quality dimension of the film that plausibly drives dissatisfaction. It is a candidate cause, not a common cause of another treatment and the outcome, so it functions as a parallel treatment rather than a confounder.

per_column.name: character_development_quality
per_column.rationale: Another film-quality attribute plausibly causing dissatisfaction. Like the others it is a candidate cause of the outcome, not a common cause of a treatment and the outcome.

judge.rationale: The added columns supply several plausible candidate causes (treatments) of audience dissatisfaction—writing quality, plot originality, character development—all surfaced from the review text. However, they are essentially parallel outcome-quality features rather than a designated treatment plus adjustment set. Crucially, NO confounders are provided: there is no variable that plausibly causes both one of these quality attributes AND dissatisfaction and would need to be adjusted for (e.g., genre, budget, reviewer expectation/predisposition, star popularity, prior franchise attachment). Without any confounders, the added columns do not set up a valid causal ESTIMATION and cannot deliver unbiased attribution. The decisive test (surfacing genuine common causes not named in the query) is not met because there are zero confounders at all.
